Downtown Jacksonville, the blue Main Street Bridge and the St. Johns River from the air (oblique helicopter-style view, not map-like): the city's most recognisable combination, sharp and in daylight; the 16:10 crop keeps bridge and towers.

alt_overrides.alt: People strolling past brick buildings and cafe awnings under shade trees in Market Square, downtown Knoxville.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Market Square is the heart of downtown Knoxville and a famous district; the current photo is daylight, leafy and lively without any person as the subject (passers-by are small). The Sunsphere/riverfront skyline would be the alternative, but this already works as a card.

alt_overrides.alt: Downtown Lancaster's rooftops, the Griest Building tower and a green copper cupola under a blue summer sky.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. The current photo (also the Wikipedia article's lead image) is a clear-day view over downtown Lancaster's rooftops to the Marriott/convention-centre tower, the Griest Building and a green copper cupola: recognisably Lancaster, sharp enough (2011x1114 original) and it centre-crops well to 16:10. Commons has nothing clearly better: the Central Market photos are a tight facade crop (CC BY-SA 3.0) or an interior (public domain), the Watt & Shand/Marriott photos are single buildings, and there are no daylight Penn Square or King Street views. Current licence CC BY-SA 3.0.

alt_overrides.alt: The domed Michigan State Capitol in Lansing under a clear blue sky, with the Austin Blair statue at right.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Current photo (Andrew Martin, CC BY 3.0) shows Lansing's signature landmark, the Michigan State Capitol, sharp under a clear blue sky; the statue beside it is the 1898 Austin Blair monument (not recent). Note the 16:7 band trims the top of the dome's lantern.

alt_overrides.alt: Downtown Little Rock towers with the Arkansas River and its bridges beyond, seen from above on a clear day.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Elevated oblique view (not map-like) of the downtown Little Rock skyline with the Arkansas River and its bridges behind, clear daylight, sharp; shows the city as people picture it and crops well.

alt_overrides.alt: Brick storefronts and mid-rise towers along a quiet street in downtown Longview, Texas, on a sunny day.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Current photo (downtown Longview street with brick storefronts and the mid-rise towers, sunny with clouds) is as representative as anything on Commons: Longview has no landmark skyline, and the alternatives (Depot Park, alleys, a brick star in the pavement, single buildings) are weaker. Crops fine to 16:10. Weakness: the empty street fills the lower third and a few cars are parked along the kerb.

Representative and sharp: downtown Manchester’s towers rising beyond the brick Millyard mill buildings, in daylight. The only public-domain/CC0 alternative found (a rooftop view from Manchester West High School) is weaker, so it was set aside (renamed _x_rejected).

alt_overrides.alt: Downtown Memphis's skyline above the Mississippi River and its sandy riverbank on a clear day.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Downtown skyline above the Mississippi River in clear daylight; the defining view of Memphis, crops cleanly.

alt_overrides.alt: The white historic Tioga Hotel with tall palm trees on a sunny day in downtown Merced.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. The current photo of the historic Tioga Hotel (1920s, National Register) on Main Street with palm trees under a blue sky is sharp and inviting; the alternatives on Commons (the 1875 County Courthouse half-hidden by trees on a grey day, or Main Street under traffic lights) are weaker. It is a single building, but a downtown landmark rather than an unremarkable one.

alt_overrides.alt: Milwaukee's downtown towers above the snowy lakefront, with the winged Milwaukee Art Museum on Lake Michigan.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Shows everything people recognise in Milwaukee in one frame: the downtown skyline (with the new Northwestern Mutual tower), the lakefront, the Calatrava-winged Art Museum and the harbour, sharp at 1920x1277. It is an oblique elevated (drone-style) view in winter, not a map-like aerial. Ground-level summer alternatives if wanted: File:Milwaukee July 2025 5 (skyline and Milwaukee Art Museum).jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, Michael Barera; big lawn foreground) and File:Milwaukee March 2024 4 (Milwaukee skyline and Milwaukee River).jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, Michael Barera; City Hall tower over the river).

The current photo is the recognisable Minneapolis skyline above the Mississippi River and a bridge, in clear daylight (winter, bare trees); sharp, landscape, and the 16:10 centre crop keeps the towers. Current licence CC BY-SA 4.0.

alt_overrides.alt: Downtown Mobile's skyline, led by the spired RSA Battle House Tower, under a clear blue sky.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. alt_overrides.alt: Downtown New Haven's towers rising above tree-filled neighborhoods in autumn color, with low hills on the horizon.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Current photo is a high, sharp view of downtown New Haven's towers above tree-filled neighbourhoods in autumn colour with hills behind; it reads as a skyline (horizon and sky, not map-like) and the 2:1 frame centre-crops cleanly to 16:10. Yale's Harkness Tower or the Green's churches would be the other choices, but this already says 'New Haven' at card size.

alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Manhattan and the Empire State Building: already representative.

It is a drone view but oblique and scenic, not map-like; the 16:10 crop keeps harbour and downtown. Current licence CC BY 4.0.

alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. No search needed.

Current photo is Wharf Street in the Old Port: cobblestones, brick warehouses and shop signs, the city's signature district; landscape, crops fine. Weakness: heavy HDR processing and an overcast sky. Alternative if Nathan prefers the region's most famous image: File:Portland Head Light, Maine's oldest lighthouse (36351593492).jpg (Portland Head Light in sun, but it stands in Cape Elizabeth, not Portland).

alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. Current photo (Abhiram Juvvadi, CC BY-SA 4.0) is a sharp elevated view of the whole downtown Raleigh skyline above green trees in warm late-afternoon daylight; representative and crops well.

alt_overrides.alt: Downtown Reno's towers glowing in golden-hour light beneath snow-capped mountains, seen across a sagebrush hillside.
alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card. alt_overrides.why: After the Phase 5 report (Nathan, 2026-10-08): the most representative photograph of each city for its home-page card.
